## ECG-AIM and the registered claim chain

ECG-AIM is the project's novel tokenized transformer reconstructor. The locked
three-lead contract observes **I, II, and V2**, reconstructs all twelve leads,
and evaluates reconstruction metrics on the nine missing leads so passthrough
cannot inflate the score. Its evidence chain is:

`PTB-XL reconstruction → clinical biomarkers → LUDB expert morphology → RDB rhythm-diverse morphology → blinded delineation`.

MCMA-U-Net, cNVAE, and MSVAE are architecture controls; ECG-AIM is not declared
superior merely because it is novel. Architecture, objective, mask, and seed
remain separate factors in all comparisons.

## Model-performance UMAP

The embedding below uses the 160-row PreSACan model summaries. It is a compact
map of multimetric behavior, useful for finding clusters, near-duplicates, and
outliers. It is not an embedding of ECG waveforms or ECG-AIM tokens.

```{python}
#| label: clinical-performance-umap
pm_metrics = numeric_metrics(presacan)
pm_matrix = model_metric_matrix(presacan, "model_id", pm_metrics)
embedding, embedding_method = performance_embedding(pm_matrix, EMBED_SEED)
if not embedding.empty:
    labels = presacan[["model_id", "dataset"]].drop_duplicates("model_id") if "dataset" in presacan else presacan[["model_id"]]
    embedding = embedding.merge(labels, on="model_id", how="left")
    embedding["family"] = embedding.model_id.str.extract(r"^([^_]+)")[0]
    fig = px.scatter(embedding, x="axis_1", y="axis_2", color="family",
                     hover_name="model_id", hover_data=[c for c in ("dataset",) if c in embedding],
                     title=f"{embedding_method} of standardized clinical-performance vectors")
    fig.update_traces(marker={"size": 9, "opacity": .8})
    fig.show()
```

## True checkpoint-activation UMAP

Unlike the preceding performance map, this optional block runs ECG records
through the checkpoint selected from `results/checkpoint_store/catalog.sqlite`,
captures an internal encoder activation, pools it per record, and embeds those
vectors. The storage layer verifies the materialized checkpoint against the
catalog SHA-256 before inference. Nothing is written to the results databases.

### 1. Choose a registered checkpoint

The table below is read without materializing any checkpoint. `local_available`
distinguishes a file that is already on disk from a remotely verified artifact
that will be downloaded only when the opt-in block runs.

```{python}
#| label: checkpoint-catalog-browser
from pathlib import Path
catalog = read_sql(ROOT / "results/checkpoint_store/catalog.sqlite", """
    select model_id, factorial_mask, seed, local_path, size_bytes, sha256,
           status, asset_state, round_trip_verified_at, metadata_json
    from checkpoints order by model_id
""")
if not catalog.empty:
    catalog["architecture"] = catalog.metadata_json.map(
        lambda raw: json.loads(raw or "{}").get("family", "unknown")
    )
    catalog["local_available"] = catalog.local_path.fillna("").map(
        lambda value: bool(value) and Path(value).is_file()
    )
    catalog["size_mb"] = (catalog.size_bytes / 2**20).round(1)
    display(catalog[["model_id", "architecture", "factorial_mask", "seed",
                     "status", "local_available", "size_mb",
                     "round_trip_verified_at", "sha256"]])
```

### 2. Choose the representation level

The hook layer changes the scientific question. Earlier layers emphasize local
wave shape, the encoder output combines long-range information, and decoder
layers increasingly reflect the reconstruction objective.

| Architecture | Recommended starting layer | Expected tensor semantics | Suggested use |
|---|---|---|---|
| ECG-AIM | `encoder` | temporal transformer tokens × model width | primary learned-representation analysis |
| MCMA-U-Net | `down5` | deepest convolutional feature map | architecture-control comparison |
| MSVAE | `encoder` | variational encoder representation | stochastic/variational comparison |

For ECG-AIM, `encoder.layers.3` and `encoder.layers.7` provide useful middle and
final-depth contrasts. Do not compare raw UMAP axes from two independently fit
embeddings: UMAP can rotate, reflect, and deform its coordinates. Use identical
records and parameters, then compare neighborhood membership, rhythm mixing,
or fit a joint/aligned analysis.

### 3. Extract, pool, and embed

For a tensor with a feature channel and a token/time dimension, the extractor
concatenates each feature's mean, standard deviation, and maximum. This retains
more information than global averaging while producing a fixed-length vector.
The standardized vectors are embedded with cosine UMAP. The default CPU device
protects concurrent training; GPU use must be explicitly enabled.

```{python}
#| label: checkpoint-activation-umap
if RUN_CHECKPOINT_UMAP:
    from checkpoint_embeddings import checkpoint_umap
    latent_umap, latent_provenance = checkpoint_umap(
        CHECKPOINT_MODEL_ID,
        ROOT / "data/rdb_wavelet_delineation_cache/test",
        layer=CHECKPOINT_LAYER,
        max_records=CHECKPOINT_RECORDS,
        batch_size=8,
        device=CHECKPOINT_DEVICE,
        seed=EMBED_SEED,
    )
    display(pd.DataFrame([latent_provenance]))
    display(latent_umap.label.value_counts().rename_axis("rhythm").reset_index(name="records"))
    fig = px.scatter(latent_umap, x="umap_1", y="umap_2", color="label",
                     hover_name="record_id", title=(
                         f"Checkpoint activation UMAP · {CHECKPOINT_MODEL_ID} · {CHECKPOINT_LAYER}"
                     ))
    fig.update_traces(marker={"size": 8, "opacity": .75})
    fig.show()
    centroids = latent_umap.groupby("label")[["umap_1", "umap_2"]].agg(["mean", "std", "count"])
    display(centroids)
    display(latent_umap[["record_id", "patient_id", "label", "nearest_record_id",
                         "nearest_label", "nearest_cosine_distance"]]
            .sort_values("nearest_cosine_distance").head(40))
else:
    display(pd.DataFrame([{
        "status": "opt-in",
        "how_to_run": "Set RUN_CHECKPOINT_UMAP=True in the controls cell and rerender this chapter",
        "model_id": CHECKPOINT_MODEL_ID,
        "layer": CHECKPOINT_LAYER,
    }]))
```

### 4. Diagnose before interpreting

When enabled, the provenance table reports:

- **Trustworthiness:** whether local high-dimensional neighbors remain local in
  the 2-D map. It evaluates projection fidelity, not biological correctness.
- **Rhythm silhouette:** separation of released rhythm groups in the original
  standardized activation space. Positive values indicate greater between-group
  than within-group separation; class imbalance and dataset confounding remain.
- **Nearest-neighbor label agreement:** a descriptive local-purity measure.
  It is not a held-out classifier score.

Inspect the nearest-neighbor table for same-patient leakage, duplicated signals,
outliers, or separation driven entirely by one rhythm. A visually clean cluster
is hypothesis-generating until confirmed by patient-level resampling and a
prespecified probe evaluated on held-out patients.

### 5. Recommended checkpoint comparisons

For an architecture comparison, keep the RDB record inventory, preprocessing,
pooling, UMAP seed, and layer depth as comparable as the architectures permit.
For a loss or wavelet ablation, keep architecture and hook layer exactly fixed.
Report at minimum:

1. checkpoint ID and SHA-256;
2. factorial mask, seed, observed leads, and architecture;
3. record and patient counts by rhythm;
4. activation shape and pooling rule;
5. UMAP parameters and trustworthiness;
6. nearest-neighbor agreement with patient-level uncertainty;
7. sensitivity to at least three UMAP seeds and reasonable neighborhood sizes.

## Overnight checkpoint-representation study

The interactive single-checkpoint block above is useful for exploration. The
production analysis is a separate resumable runner so a browser render cannot
accidentally download checkpoints, consume the training GPU, or leave a partial
wide table. Its authoritative protocol is frozen at
`refine-logs/EXPERIMENT_PLAN.md`; the clinically relevant claim map, endpoints,
predictor ladder, uncertainty, multiplicity, and stopping rules are reproduced
in this deployed chapter so the published analysis has no out-of-tree resource
dependency.

The production design is motivated by the spatial-reconstruction/QT multitask
logic of [Ansari et al.'s 3DRECON-QT study](https://doi.org/10.1161/CIRCULATIONAHA.125.077494)
and the discrimination, calibration, validation, and clinician-confirmation
principles in the [2023 ACC/AHA/ACCP/HRS AF guideline](https://doi.org/10.1161/CIR.0000000000001193).
It uses one CPU core and compact SQLite storage. A0 and the
enhanced ECG-AIM checkpoint use all 2,398 RDB train/validation/test records; a
frozen nine-checkpoint panel uses the identical 360-record test inventory. Each
feature row is bound to checkpoint SHA-256, record-manifest SHA-256, layer, and
pooling version. UMAP is descriptive; probes and ORs use the original pooled
encoder activations.

```{python}
#| label: checkpoint-study-live-status
STUDY_DB = ROOT / "results/checkpoint_embeddings/compact.sqlite"
display(source_inventory({"checkpoint representation study": STUDY_DB}))
study_jobs = read_sql(STUDY_DB, "select * from jobs order by started_at, model_id")
if study_jobs.empty:
    display(pd.DataFrame([{"status": "initialized or waiting for first checkpoint",
                           "monitor": "tmux capture-pane -p -t checkpoint_embedding_rdb"}]))
else:
    study_jobs["progress_percent"] = 100 * study_jobs.completed_records / study_jobs.expected_records
    display(study_jobs[["model_id", "checkpoint_sha256", "split_scope", "layer",
                        "status", "completed_records", "expected_records",
                        "progress_percent", "started_at", "completed_at", "error"]])
    fig = px.bar(study_jobs, x="progress_percent", y="model_id", color="status",
                 orientation="h", range_x=[0,100], hover_data=["completed_records","expected_records"],
                 title="Resumable checkpoint activation extraction")
    fig.show()
```

### Held-out probe and association results

These tables populate only after a checkpoint passes its exact record-count and
feature-shape gate. ORs are per-standard-deviation cross-sectional score
associations with code-level outcomes—not causal effects, incidence estimates,
risk ratios, or treatment recommendations.

```{python}
#| label: checkpoint-study-probes
probe = read_sql(STUDY_DB, "select * from probe_results")
odds = read_sql(STUDY_DB, "select * from odds_ratios")
if probe.empty:
    display(pd.DataFrame([{"status": "pending complete extraction and analysis"}]))
else:
    display(probe.sort_values(["outcome","predictor_set","metric"]))
if not odds.empty:
    display(odds.sort_values(["outcome","predictor_set","term"]))
    finite_or = odds.replace([np.inf,-np.inf],np.nan).dropna(subset=["odds_ratio","ci_low","ci_high"])
    if not finite_or.empty:
        fig = px.scatter(finite_or, x="odds_ratio", y="predictor_set", color="outcome",
                         error_x=finite_or.ci_high-finite_or.odds_ratio,
                         error_x_minus=finite_or.odds_ratio-finite_or.ci_low,
                         log_x=True, title="Exploratory score association ORs (95% CI)")
        fig.add_vline(x=1, line_dash="dash", line_color="black")
        fig.show()
```

### Prespecified estimands and model ladder

The primary endpoint is **AF/AFIB-coded membership**, not adjudicated clinical
AF. Every predictor follows the same Occam-constrained ladder: intercept-only,
three waveform summaries, one latent principal component, validation-selected
latent PCs from `{1, 2, 4, 8}`, and waveform summaries plus the selected PCs.
Imputation, scaling, PCA, penalties, and probability calibration are learned
without the test split. The final 360-record test split is evaluated once.

The table below combines discrimination, calibration, and absolute-risk
separation. A useful embedding should improve paired AUROC/AUPRC while reducing
Brier score and log loss; a high AUROC paired with a poor calibration slope is
not sufficient. Confidence intervals use 2,000 stratified cached-record
bootstraps. Because the current cache has one row per cached patient/record ID,
this is not proof that the source cohort contains no repeated person.

```{python}
#| label: rigorous-heldout-results
extended = read_sql_optional(STUDY_DB, "select * from extended_results")
if extended.empty:
    display(pd.DataFrame([{"status":"pending rigorous post-analysis",
                           "stage":"runs automatically after extraction"}]))
else:
    model_key = read_sql(STUDY_DB, "select job_id,model_id from jobs")
    extended = extended.merge(model_key, on="job_id", how="left")
    display(extended.sort_values(["outcome","model_id","predictor_set","metric"]))
    focus = extended.query("outcome == 'AF_AFIB_code_membership' and metric in ['auroc','auprc','brier','log_loss']")
    if not focus.empty:
        fig = px.bar(focus, x="value", y="model_id", color="predictor_set",
                     facet_col="metric", barmode="group", orientation="h",
                     error_x=focus.ci_high-focus.value,
                     error_x_minus=focus.value-focus.ci_low,
                     title="Held-out discrimination and error with 95% bootstrap CIs")
        fig.update_xaxes(matches=None)
        fig.show()
```

### Held-out ROC, precision–recall, and calibration curves

Curves are reconstructed from persisted test probabilities, not from UMAP
coordinates or resubstitution predictions. The intercept-only rung exposes
prevalence, the waveform rung is the parsimonious comparator, and latent gains
are interpreted only when paired uncertainty agrees across discrimination and
proper scoring rules.

```{python}
#| label: binary-curves
binary_pred = read_sql_optional(STUDY_DB,"select * from binary_predictions")
if binary_pred.empty:
    display(pd.DataFrame([{"status":"pending held-out binary probabilities"}]))
else:
    from sklearn.metrics import roc_curve,precision_recall_curve
    from sklearn.calibration import calibration_curve
    model_key=read_sql(STUDY_DB,"select job_id,model_id from jobs")
    binary_pred=binary_pred.merge(model_key,on="job_id",how="left")
    roc_rows=[];pr_rows=[];cal_rows=[]
    for (model,predictor),g in binary_pred.groupby(["model_id","predictor_set"]):
        fpr,tpr,_=roc_curve(g.truth,g.probability)
        precision,recall,_=precision_recall_curve(g.truth,g.probability)
        obs,forecast=calibration_curve(g.truth,g.probability,n_bins=10,strategy="quantile")
        key=f"{model} · {predictor}"
        roc_rows.extend({"curve":key,"fpr":a,"tpr":b} for a,b in zip(fpr,tpr))
        pr_rows.extend({"curve":key,"recall":a,"precision":b} for a,b in zip(recall,precision))
        cal_rows.extend({"curve":key,"predicted":a,"observed":b} for a,b in zip(forecast,obs))
    fig=go.Figure()
    for key,g in pd.DataFrame(roc_rows).groupby("curve"):fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(x=g.fpr,y=g.tpr,name=key,mode="lines"))
    fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(x=[0,1],y=[0,1],name="chance",line={"dash":"dash","color":"black"}))
    fig.update_layout(title="Held-out AF/AFIB-code ROC",xaxis_title="False-positive rate",yaxis_title="True-positive rate");fig.show()
    fig=px.line(pd.DataFrame(pr_rows),x="recall",y="precision",color="curve",title="Held-out AF/AFIB-code precision–recall");fig.show()
    cal=pd.DataFrame(cal_rows);fig=px.line(cal,x="predicted",y="observed",color="curve",markers=True,title="Held-out probability calibration")
    fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(x=[0,1],y=[0,1],name="ideal",line={"dash":"dash","color":"black"}));fig.show()

predictor_delta=read_sql_optional(STUDY_DB,"select * from predictor_comparisons")
if not predictor_delta.empty:
    model_key=read_sql(STUDY_DB,"select job_id,model_id from jobs")
    predictor_delta=predictor_delta.merge(model_key,on="job_id",how="left")
    display(predictor_delta.sort_values(["outcome","model_id","reference_set","candidate_set","metric"]))
```

### Matched checkpoint effects and multiplicity

Checkpoint comparisons are paired by exact RDB record ID. `delta_b_minus_a`
therefore estimates the enhanced-minus-A0 change under the same inventory,
pooling, probe class, validation selection, and bootstrap draw. Positive is
better for AUROC/AUPRC; negative is better for Brier/log loss. Raw and
Holm-adjusted values are both retained so multiplicity is visible rather than
silently hidden.

```{python}
#| label: rigorous-paired-checkpoints
checkpoint_delta = read_sql_optional(STUDY_DB, "select * from paired_comparisons")
multiplicity = read_sql_optional(STUDY_DB, "select * from multiplicity_results")
if checkpoint_delta.empty:
    display(pd.DataFrame([{"status":"pending both complete full-cohort checkpoints"}]))
else:
    display(checkpoint_delta.sort_values(["outcome","metric"]))
    display(multiplicity.sort_values(["family","adjusted_p"]))
    fig = px.scatter(checkpoint_delta, x="delta_b_minus_a", y="metric", color="outcome",
                     error_x=checkpoint_delta.ci_high-checkpoint_delta.delta_b_minus_a,
                     error_x_minus=checkpoint_delta.delta_b_minus_a-checkpoint_delta.ci_low,
                     title="Enhanced minus A0: paired held-out effects")
    fig.add_vline(x=0,line_dash="dash",line_color="black")
    fig.show()
```

### Repolarization-content agreement

The repolarization endpoint is the annotation-derived interval from QRS onset
to the subsequent T offset. It is reported in milliseconds but is **not** a
clinical QT or QTc measurement. The probe ladder is compared against a
mean-only predictor and the same three-summary waveform baseline. Alongside
MAE/RMSE and correlation, the analysis reports Lin concordance, calibration,
and Bland–Altman bias and limits of agreement. These detect scale or offset
errors that correlation alone can conceal.

```{python}
#| label: repolarization-agreement
if not extended.empty:
    rep = extended.query("outcome == 'annotation_QRSon_Toff_ms'")
    if not rep.empty:
        display(rep.sort_values(["model_id","predictor_set","metric"]))

rep_pred = read_sql_optional(STUDY_DB, "select * from regression_predictions")
if rep_pred.empty:
    display(pd.DataFrame([{"status":"pending annotation-derived duration probes"}]))
else:
    model_key = read_sql(STUDY_DB, "select job_id,model_id from jobs")
    rep_pred = rep_pred.merge(model_key,on="job_id",how="left")
    shown = rep_pred.query("predictor_set == 'latent'").copy()
    shown["pair_mean_ms"] = (shown.truth + shown.prediction)/2
    shown["prediction_minus_truth_ms"] = shown.prediction-shown.truth
    fig = px.scatter(shown,x="pair_mean_ms",y="prediction_minus_truth_ms",color="model_id",
                     hover_name="record_id",marginal_y="histogram",
                     title="Annotation-derived QRSon–Toff Bland–Altman view")
    fig.add_hline(y=0,line_dash="dash",line_color="black")
    fig.show()
```

### Eight-code rhythm sensitivity analysis

This is secondary and code-level. The multinomial penalty and latent dimension
are selected by validation log loss, then frozen for test. Macro metrics prevent
the 60-record groups from completely dominating AT (18), ST (21), and SVT (21),
but those rare-code rows remain descriptive rather than independent clinical
claims. Row-normalized confusion matrices show *which* rhythm codes exchange
errors instead of compressing behavior into one accuracy number.

```{python}
#| label: rhythm-code-analysis
multi = read_sql_optional(STUDY_DB,"select * from multiclass_results")
conf = read_sql_optional(STUDY_DB,"select * from confusion_matrix")
if multi.empty:
    display(pd.DataFrame([{"status":"pending complete full-cohort checkpoint"}]))
else:
    model_key=read_sql(STUDY_DB,"select job_id,model_id from jobs")
    multi=multi.merge(model_key,on="job_id",how="left")
    display(multi.sort_values(["model_id","class_label","metric"]))
    cm=conf.merge(model_key,on="job_id",how="left")
    selected=cm.model_id.iloc[-1]
    mat=cm[cm.model_id.eq(selected)].pivot(index="true_label",columns="predicted_label",values="row_fraction")
    fig=px.imshow(mat,text_auto=".2f",aspect="auto",zmin=0,zmax=1,
                  title=f"Row-normalized test confusion matrix · {selected}")
    fig.show()
```

### Reconstruction quality-control odds ratio

For a checkpoint with an exact SHA match in the RDB oracle, failure is frozen
from validation data as missing-precordial Pearson below its 10th percentile or
MSE above its 90th percentile. The predictor is a train-fitted eight-PC
Ledoit–Wolf Mahalanobis outlier score. The reported OR is the cross-sectional
odds of measured reconstruction failure per one training-standard-deviation
increase in that score. It is a model quality-control association—not patient
prognosis, AF incidence, or treatment benefit.

```{python}
#| label: reconstruction-failure-or
qc_or = odds.query("outcome == 'reconstruction_failure'").copy() if not odds.empty else pd.DataFrame()
qc_risk = extended.query("outcome == 'reconstruction_failure'").copy() if not extended.empty else pd.DataFrame()
if qc_or.empty:
    display(pd.DataFrame([{"status":"pending SHA-matched enhanced-checkpoint embeddings"}]))
else:
    display(qc_or)
    display(qc_risk)
    fig=px.scatter(qc_or,x="odds_ratio",y="predictor_set",error_x=qc_or.ci_high-qc_or.odds_ratio,
                   error_x_minus=qc_or.odds_ratio-qc_or.ci_low,log_x=True,
                   title="Reconstruction-failure OR per SD latent outlier score")
    fig.add_vline(x=1,line_dash="dash",line_color="black")
    fig.show()
```

### Projection stability and live UMAP

The production grid fixes five seeds and neighborhood sizes 10, 30, and 60.
Trustworthiness, high-dimensional rhythm-code silhouette, and nearest-code
agreement are displayed together so cluster appearance is never the sole result.

```{python}
#| label: checkpoint-study-stability
diag = read_sql(STUDY_DB, "select * from diagnostics")
if not diag.empty:
    display(diag.sort_values(["job_id","split","seed","neighbors","metric"]))
    stable = diag.query("analysis == 'umap' and split == 'test'")
    if not stable.empty:
        fig = px.line(stable, x="neighbors", y="value", color="metric",
                      line_group="job_id", facet_col="metric", markers=True,
                      title="Test projection diagnostics across fixed UMAP seeds")
        fig.update_yaxes(matches=None)
        fig.show()

projection = read_sql(STUDY_DB, """
    select p.*,r.canonical_rhythm,r.released_rhythm,r.patient_id,j.model_id
    from projections p join records r using(record_id) join jobs j using(job_id)
    where p.seed=42 and p.neighbors=30 and r.split='test'
""")
if not projection.empty:
    chosen_model = projection.model_id.iloc[-1]
    shown = projection[projection.model_id == chosen_model]
    fig = px.scatter(shown, x="x", y="y", color="canonical_rhythm",
                     hover_name="record_id", hover_data=["patient_id","released_rhythm"],
                     title=f"Train-fit/test-transform encoder UMAP · {chosen_model}")
    fig.update_traces(marker={"size":8,"opacity":.75})
    fig.show()
```

### Cross-checkpoint representation agreement

Raw UMAP axes cannot be compared between checkpoints. Instead, the post-analysis
uses the identical 360 test records and reports linear centered-kernel alignment
(CKA), Spearman correlation of pairwise cosine distances (RSA), and 10-neighbor
Jaccard overlap in the original standardized features. These answer distinct
questions: shared linear geometry, shared global ordering, and shared local
neighborhoods. Agreement alone does not tell us which representation is better;
it localizes whether a performance difference reflects a genuinely changed
latent geometry.

```{python}
#| label: checkpoint-geometry
similarity = read_sql_optional(STUDY_DB, "select * from checkpoint_similarity")
if similarity.empty:
    display(pd.DataFrame([{"status":"pending two or more completed checkpoints"}]))
else:
    model_key = read_sql(STUDY_DB, "select job_id,model_id from jobs")
    names = dict(zip(model_key.job_id,model_key.model_id))
    similarity["checkpoint_a"] = similarity.job_a.map(names)
    similarity["checkpoint_b"] = similarity.job_b.map(names)
    similarity["contrast"] = similarity.checkpoint_a + " ↔ " + similarity.checkpoint_b
    display(similarity.sort_values(["metric","value"],ascending=[True,False]))
    fig = px.imshow(similarity.pivot(index="contrast",columns="metric",values="value"),
                    aspect="auto",color_continuous_scale="Viridis",
                    title="Matched test-set representation agreement")
    fig.show()

umap_pair_stability = read_sql_optional(STUDY_DB, "select * from umap_stability")
if not umap_pair_stability.empty:
    display(umap_pair_stability.groupby(["job_id","split","metric"]).value
            .agg(["mean","std","min","max","count"]).reset_index())
```

### Reproducible nearest-neighbor inspection

The compact database intentionally stores no waveform CSV. To inspect a point,
choose a checkpoint and record from the UMAP, retrieve its nearest neighbors by
cosine distance from the compressed feature blobs, and then load the original
cached `.pt` records for waveform display. This preserves one source of truth
while keeping the analysis modular: change the checkpoint, rhythm filter,
neighbor count, seed, or UMAP neighborhood in the controls and rerender.

Operationally, the study is safe to interrupt by creating
`results/checkpoint_embeddings/STOP`. Each record is committed transactionally;
removing the sentinel and rerunning the recorded command resumes missing rows.
The production worker pauses below 3 GiB available RAM or 8 GiB free disk and
never uses the training GPU.

### Clinical interpretation boundary

RDB cannot support the outcome model in Ansari et al. because it contains no
drug exposure or longitudinal ventricular-arrhythmia outcome. It also cannot
support AHA-guideline stroke-risk or anticoagulation decisions because age,
sex, comorbidity, AF burden, and outcomes are absent. This analysis can show
that a representation retains code-associated rhythm/repolarization morphology
and may support reconstruction quality control. Confirmatory clinical utility
requires an external patient-level cohort with adjudicated outcomes.

## LUDB and RDB blinded delineation

```{python}
#| label: blinded-load
le, lb = load_blinded(LUDB_BLIND, "LUDB")
re, rb = load_blinded(RDB_BLIND, "RDB")
blinded_eval = pd.concat([le, re], ignore_index=True)
boundaries = pd.concat([lb, rb], ignore_index=True)
display(blinded_eval.sort_values(["cohort", "primary_mean_micro_f1_20ms"], ascending=[True, False]))
```

```{python}
#| label: blinded-boundary-heatmap
for cohort, frame in boundaries.groupby("cohort"):
    if "lead_group" in frame and (frame.lead_group == RDB_LEAD_GROUP).any():
        frame = frame[frame.lead_group == RDB_LEAD_GROUP]
    pivot = frame.pivot_table(index="model_id", columns="boundary", values="micro_f1_20ms")
    if not pivot.empty:
        fig = px.imshow(pivot, zmin=0, zmax=1, color_continuous_scale="Viridis",
                        aspect="auto", title=f"{cohort}: blinded boundary F1 within 20 ms")
        fig.update_layout(height=max(450, 18 * len(pivot)))
        fig.show()
```

RDB has six genuine supervised boundary channels: P-on, P-off, QRS-on,
QRS-off, T-on, and T-off. Peak channels are not fabricated. Consequently,
onset/offset findings are valid targets; a T-peak claim is not.

```{python}
#| label: protocol-consistency
cross = re.query("status == 'complete'").merge(oracle.query("status == 'complete'"), on="model_id", suffixes=("_blind", "_oracle"))
oracle_x = next((c for c in ["metric.signal_pearson_p05", "metric.missing_signal_pearson_p05"] if c in cross), None)
if not cross.empty and oracle_x:
    fig = px.scatter(cross, x=oracle_x, y="primary_mean_micro_f1_20ms",
                     hover_name="model_id", color="factorial_mask_blind",
                     title="RDB oracle signal tail versus blinded boundary preservation")
    fig.show()
```

## Interpretation discipline

For every apparent winner report: **observation with raw numbers → uncertainty
or replication status → narrow interpretation → falsification experiment**.
Agreement across reconstruction, clinical endpoints, oracle morphology, and
blinded delineation is stronger than winning any one leaderboard.
